passing: Retain contextual references without manufacturing source positions.
brief: Retain the spoken view and its immediate qualifiers without inventing details.
substantive: Preserve conclusion, mechanism, meaningful conditions, limitations and source confidence.
deep: Preserve the full reasoning chain, positive and negative paths, relevant comparisons, context, disagreements and uncertainty.
structural: Preserve the broader game or weekly strategy independently of any one player; link affected subjects and conditions.

title: NFL Game / Matchup Preview
description: Week-scoped game-by-game NFL previews preserving winner picks, opposing-unit interactions, game script, key player roles and host differences.
principles: Preserve every substantively covered game; do not omit late games or the initial separate news block.
A matchup take records a time-scoped opinion, not a timeless team fact or actual result.
Preserve each host's pick and reasoning when attributable; never generate an artificial consensus.
Connect the game-level thesis to independent player, team, coaching and scheme takes when the source supports both.
Only store numerical scores, win probabilities, spreads or specific production forecasts if actually stated.
Season/week identify applicability; canonical game IDs only when confirmed, never guessed.

dimensions.description: season, NFL week, opponent pairing and game identity
dimensions.preservation_expectation: Identify both teams and the relevant game window; do not invent a canonical ID.
detection_questions: Did the source materially discuss season, nfl week, opponent pairing and game identity?
What reasoning, conditions or uncertainty were expressed?

review_questions: Does every substantively covered game retain season/week and teams?
Can readers reconstruct winner picks and the rationale for the predicted game flow?
Are opposing units, coach/scheme mechanics, uncertainty and injury conditions preserved when discussed?
Were hosts' differences and late-game segments retained?
Are game-wide forecasts and player-level implications reusable without merging them?
forbidden_distortions: Never invent a winner, projected score, spread or percentage.
Never retroactively rewrite the original forecast using the actual game outcome.
Never treat a team's predicted win as a player start recommendation.
Never guess speaker identity, canonical game ID or injury certainty.
Never omit entire games just because the episode's main headline covers another matchup.
extension_signals: Repeated betting/spread forecasts need additional dimensions.
Post-game film-review episodes expose distinct recap needs.
Repeatedly used game identities exceed the current weekly_context contract.
